chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Isa ibn Yunus, from al-Awza'i, from al-Zuhri, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), who said:
It is not permissible for the captive to marry while in the hands of the polytheists, for fear that he may have a child with her, and the child remains a disbeliever in their hands.

And he said: When you take a captive who is unable to walk and you do not have a mount with you, then release him and do not kill him, for you do not know what the ruling of the Imam will be regarding him.
And he said: The captive, when he embraces Islam, his blood is secured (not to be killed) and he becomes spoils of war (bayt al-mal).

key_terms.الْمُشْرِكِينَ: Polytheists (those who associate partners with God)
key_terms.حُقِنَ دَمُهُ: His blood was secured (protected from being killed)

ai.seo_question: What are the legal rulings for prisoners of war regarding marriage, release, and conversion in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ali (AS) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes key jurisprudential principles regarding the treatment of prisoners of war, emphasizing the precautionary measure of preventing apostasy through marriage with polytheists. It highlights the concept of *tadabbur* (deliberation) in military command, where a captor releases an incapacitated prisoner due to uncertainty about the Imam's final ruling, and affirms that conversion secures the captive's blood and status as *fay'* (booty/public treasury).
